best_practices: Rinse out food and liquid residues thoroughly.
Keep plastic caps screwed on bottles so they don't fall through sorting screens.
Do NOT place plastic bags in curbside bins (they tangle in sorting machinery).
Avoid black plastics as optical sorting infrared sensors often fail to detect carbon black pigment.
Rinse jars and bottles lightly; labels do not need to be scraped off.
Separate metal and plastic lids (recycle lids in metal/plastic streams).
Never mix window panes, mirrors, drinking glasses, or Pyrex dishes with bottle glass (different melting temperatures).
Color sorting (clear, amber, green) helps maintain raw cullet value.
Rinse food tins and beverage cans to prevent odor and pest attraction.
Crush aluminum cans if your municipality allows (saves collection transport volume).
Roll clean aluminum foil into a tight ball (at least 5cm / tennis-ball diameter).
Ensure aerosol cans are completely depressurized and empty before disposal.
Keep paper dry and free of grease or cooking oil.
Small staples and paperclips are acceptable; modern hydrapulpers remove them with magnets.
Do NOT recycle thermal receipts (contain BPA/BPS coatings).
Do NOT recycle paper towels, facial tissues, or napkins (fibers are too short and often soiled).
Break down and flatten all shipping boxes to save bin space.
Remove styrofoam blocks, bubble wrap, and plastic air pillows.
For pizza boxes: tear off greasy cheese bottoms (put in trash/compost) and recycle clean tops.
Wax-coated produce boxes should go to compost or residual waste.
Bag tightly to prevent litter dispersal during municipal collection.
Never place lithium-ion batteries or electronics in household trash (fire hazard).
Compost kitchen vegetable peels, coffee grounds, and yard waste whenever possible.
Donate functional clothing, books, and household goods instead of discarding.
